title: Three rows, one list
hook: Build a grid of three empty rows, add one item to the first row. How many items does the grid hold?
concept: Repeating a mutable object does not copy it. All three rows point at the same list, so a change in one row shows up in all of them. A related trap is a default value that is created once and then shared between calls.

checks.label: Items in a 3-row grid after adding one item to row 0
Length of the list returned by the second call to add(2)

worlds.js: fill([]) puts the same array in every slot, so the grid holds 3. Default parameters are evaluated on each call, so the second check is safe.
worlds.python: [[]] * 3 repeats one list. A default argument like bucket=[] is created once at definition time, so the second call sees the first call's item.
worlds.java: Collections.nCopies repeats one list. Java has no default arguments, but a shared static list makes the same mistake.

fix: Create a fresh object per row or per call: Array.from with a factory, a list comprehension, a loop, or bucket=None and create the list inside the function.

regression.python:
def add_item(item, bucket=None):
    if bucket is None:
        bucket = []
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket


grid = [[] for _ in range(3)]
grid[0].append(1)
assert sum(len(row) for row in grid) == 1
add_item(1)
assert len(add_item(2)) == 1
